To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

QCD corrections are important in the analysis of anomalous couplings and that the dimension-5 approximation to the effective theory is inadequate to constrain anomalous couplings in the high-p T region of the LHC.

QCD corrections to anomalous W +W - production are important and can be calculated using the helicity amplitude approach; that anomalous gauge bosons and fermions can be constrained at the LHC using the helicity amplitudes; and that effective field theory is not sufficient for the analysis of W +W − production at the Lhc.
QCD corrections are large for W + W − pair production, especially for longitudinally polarized W + W − pairs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of anomalous W +W - production at the Lhc in the framework of effective field theory.
the study of the impact of anomolous couplings on W +W - production at the Lhc.
the following questions: 1) What is the impact of the QCD corrections on the anomalous couplings in the production of W+ W− pairs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHC is a very powerful machine to constrain new physics in W +W − pair production, but only if the QCD and electoweak corrections are included.

, at the LHC, the QCD corrections are important and should be included in the fits to anomolous couplings, and that the dimension-8 approximation is sufficient for constraining new physics contributions.
, at the LHC, the most sensitive channel for probing anomalous gauge bosons and fermions is W +W - production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of a signal for new physics, the current LHC measurements are consistent with the SM and the constraints on new physics couplings are not very stringent.
the W +W - production at the LEP and Tevatron experiments is sensitive to the dimension-6 effective operators, while at the LHC the dimension-8 operators become important.
the LHC can provide strong limits on anomalous W W γ and W W Z couplings, but not on anomalous fermion couplings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
QCD corrections are essential to the interpretation of W +W − production data at the LHC in the context of new physics searches.
the QCD corrections to the W +W - production process are large and cannot be neglected.
the QCD corrections are important for constraining the anomalous W W γ and W W Z couplings.
